max_tire.note: An Expedition Portal owner runs 235/85R16s on standard steel wheels on a narrow-body G, which is a sensible no-lift ceiling. Beyond that you need lift springs, and bigger tires can trigger ABS/ESP warnings on later trucks.

identify.intro: Lots of W461s are ex-military trucks, and the line between a late W460 and an early W461 is blurry. Let the chassis number decide, not the seller's description.

items.head: Chassis number
items.body: BaT-sold W461s carry the 461 model code: 1991–92 250 GD Wolfs are WDB461401…, 1993–94 290 GDs WDB46133…. Puch-badged 230 GEs use a VAG prefix (VAG461217…).

items.head: Wolf or W460?
items.body: Expedition Motor Company, which restores them, calls the 250 GD Wolf an ex-military W461, and Wikipedia lists the 1990–91 Wolf under the W461. Check the VIN and data card on the truck in front of you.

items.head: 24-volt electrics
items.body: Military W461s run 24-volt systems, and parts suppliers stock 24 V components such as blower motors. The Australian civilian Professional wagon is described as carrying two 12-volt batteries. Check before wiring in accessories.

items.head: Running gear
items.body: Wikipedia describes the W461 as the narrow W460 body with the W463 powertrain. The G 300 CDI Professional has permanent 4WD with a 50:50 split, a two-speed transfer case and three diff locks you can select on the move.

items.head: Engine swaps
items.body: OM606 and other turbodiesel conversions turn up on Bring a Trailer; two OM606-swapped 240 GDs filed there under the W461 sold for $20,500 and $55,000. Check the engine number against the model badge.

capability.note: OM642 3.0 V6 turbodiesel, G 300 CDI Professional

values.intro: Ex-military Wolfs and Puch 230 GEs have become cult trucks in the US; clean, well-documented examples and sensible turbodiesel conversions sell for the most.
values.note: Based on 31 sold Bring a Trailer auctions from January 2025 to October 2026 ($20,500–$116,000, median $54,500). Puch 230 GEs sold for $21,000–64,121 and 250 GD Wolfs for $20,500–116,000. Late Professional-series trucks almost never appear in the US.

paragraphs: The W461 was never sold new in the US, so every American example is a private import. NHTSA allows any vehicle at least 25 years old to be imported, counted from its date of manufacture and declared under Box 1 of the HS-7 form. In late 2026 that means trucks built up to late 2001: Wolfs, 230 GEs, 290 GDs and early 290 GD Turbodiesels. G 270 CDIs and later Professionals aren't eligible yet. Check your state's titling and emissions rules before you bid.

production.intro: The W461 was the G for armies, authorities and NGOs, built from 1990 until military production ended in 2022.
